items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: Trumpets: Jon Faddis, Lew Soloff, Al Rubin, Randy Brecker. ... We did sixteen takes in a three hour session.

ctx.x: “Late in the Evening” is the name of the song. Okay. Trumpets: Jon Faddis, Lew Soloff, Al Rubin, Randy Brecker. Saxes: George Young, Lou Marini, Michael Brecker, Eddie Daniels, Ronnie Cuber baritone sax. Rhythm section: Steve Gadd, Tony Levin on bass, Richard Tee on piano, Hugh McCracken on guitar. We did sixteen takes in a three hour session. That’s all we had is one chart to do.
I bet you guys played it right the first time though.

items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: the guys that played in the group Dreams with the Brecker brothers

ctx.x: I love that. That’s like, “That was perfect, let’s do it again.”

And that was the best band I ever played in, best big band that I ever played in. Trombones: well myself and Jim Pugh, Dave Taylor, Barry Rogers, the guys that played in the group Dreams with the Brecker brothers. He was the first Latin trombone player. He was the first salsa trombone player. Jewish kid from the Bronx, grew up in a Puerto Rican neighborhood. Before Barry Rogers, they only had saxophones and trumpets in salsa music and suddenly Barry came on the scene and bang, it was all over. Now every salsa…
With that Paul Simon tune, who would have been responsible for assembling that all-star group of horn players? © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
